absent: Numeric values for version bit, commands, search modes, flags, error codes and default limits.
Queue creation, identifier allocation, permission evaluation for control, and info and downcall helper internals.
Message load, store, free, sender enqueue and wakeup helper internals.
Security decision logic for send and receive.
Scheduling, wake queue mechanics, signal handling and pid and credential translation internals.
Percpu counter, RCU, spinlock, rwsem, list, bucket allocator and proc seq iteration internals.
Ucount hash sizing and function, reference lifecycle, maxima configuration and user namespace linkage beyond shown calls.

findings.text: Compat queue status layout groups a permission object, queue link placeholders, three timestamps, byte totals, short occupancy and limit counters, and sender and receiver pid markers in 32-bit compatible widths.
Compat message envelope pairs a compat-width type with trailing payload bytes.
Message payload beyond the first page is held in singly linked tail segments; usable bytes in the first chunk and in each later segment equal one page minus the corresponding header.
Initial IPC namespace statically links common namespace state with the initial user namespace.

Compat control separates legacy and extended layouts by a version bit stripped from the command; import from user only honors permission and size limit after zeroing, export to user expands permission, split timestamps, occupancy, limits and pid markers; dispatch serves info, status variants, set and remove, rejecting negative identifiers and unknown commands.

Send validates length against namespace ceiling and sign, identifier sign and positive type before lookup; receive validates identifier and length sign, demands copy mode without exception matching plus nonblocking, bounds staging length by namespace ceiling, then derives an internal selector from requested type and flags.

Type selection offers any, equal, not-equal, bounded less-equal and positional number; zero means first, negative means magnitude bound with extreme clamped, exception inverts equality, copy forces positional; queue scan honors a security check and returns first match, predecessor tracking for bounded search, or indexed element for positional search.

Result export writes type then at most the smaller of user length and stored length; duplication validates destination capacity and replicates type, length and bytes across chained chunks; alternate builds report unimplemented for staging and duplication with no-op release.

Message namespace starts with symbolic maxima for message size, queue bytes and queue count, zeroed byte and header tallies and an empty identifier set; teardown expunges every queue then destroys identifier and counter state.

Identifier table initializes empty with zero sequence, initialized lookup structures and sentinel indices showing no allocation; status display reports key, identifier, mode, occupancy, endpoint pids in viewer pid namespace, ownership in viewer user namespace and three timestamps.

Reference grab succeeds only on nonzero count; namespace charge walks ancestor counters incrementing below per-namespace maxima with rollback on failure, while release walks the same chain decrementing only when positive with warning on anomaly.

Counter entries are found by RCU hash on namespace and owner with reference acquisition; miss allocates a zeroed single-reference entry and publishes under spin protection with recheck to suppress duplicates; bounded increment uses a compare-and-swap retry loop.

Send and receive hold RCU across lookup and object lock across permission, liveness, security and capacity or search checks; blocking paths release locks for sleep, then reacquire and revalidate liveness before continuing.

Direct delivery runs under object lock, removes the chosen waiter, refreshes metadata, queues deferred wakeup and publishes the message pointer with release ordering; the receiver pairs a lockless observation with acquire ordering and a locked recheck.

Teardown serializes identifier iteration with a write lock while locking each object for destruction; counter hash serializes insertion with an interrupt-safe spin lock and lookup with RCU; accumulated wakeups flush after object lock release.
Send moves from validation to lookup to either immediate placement or sender enqueue and sleep, resuming with removal, signal and capacity rechecks until placement or error.

Receive moves from validation to lookup to immediate unlink, copy without unlink, fast absence, or receiver enqueue and sleep; wake resolves via lockless pointer test then locked confirmation distinguishing delivery, removal and interruption.

Arrival either hands off directly to a compatible waiter with sufficient room or appends to the tail updating timestamps, endpoint pid and byte, count and per-namespace tallies; non-copy removal reverses occupancy, refreshes receive metadata and wakes blocked senders.

Global init prepares the default namespace and proc view; per-namespace init brings up limits, counters and identifiers with ordered cleanup on failure; teardown reverses the order; counter entries progress from miss to allocated to published to charged, unwinding on failure or release.
Compat queue control entry pins extended version and delegates to shared compat control; legacy entry strips version from the command before delegating.
Native and compat send entries fetch the type from their respective user envelope then call shared send with payload address, length and flags.
Native and compat receive entries call shared receive with identifier, buffer, length, selector and flags, each supplying its matching fill helper for result export.
Shared kernel helpers centralize send, receive and control logic including user fetch, version handling and dispatch so syscall wrappers stay thin.

Subsystem helpers publish global and per-namespace setup and teardown, identifier setup, bulk teardown iteration, proc registration with header and display callback plus a no-op alternate, and pid namespace extraction for display.

Reference, charge and lookup helpers publish conditional reference grab, namespace charge wrappers, hierarchical increment and decrement, allocation with dedup, hash addressing, table lookup and bounded increment.
Queues may be removed concurrently with lookup or sleep; paths revalidate liveness after every reacquisition and report removal rather than using freed state.

Blocked peers abort on pending signals with restartable interruption; full queues fail fast under nonwait, empty queues report absence under nonwait, undersized buffers fail or truncate per no-error flag, and undersized direct delivery reports size error to the waiter.

Builds without copy support fail copy receives early; most negative selector is clamped to avoid negation overflow; user access faults during type fetch or result export and permission denials surface as distinct errors.
Default queue limits are named symbolic constants for largest message, largest queue contents and largest queue count.
Message chunk capacities are defined as one page minus the header of the first chunk and of later segments respectively.

Control and transfer define a version bit for extended layout, command names for info, status variants, set and remove, search selectors for any, equal, not-equal, bounded and positional, and flags for copy, exception, no-error truncation and nonwait.
Message utility owns a global spin lock and a bucket allocator for message headers created during init with accounting.
